_comment: Repository coverage policy: 100% on all four metrics, no exclusions.
'floor' is the enforced ratchet - CI fails below it. Raise it as tests land;
never lower it. 'target' is the policy itself and does not move.
Measured by istanbul (scripts/istanbul-preload.ts instruments source on load
during `bun test`), NOT by Bun's built-in coverage. Bun remains the runner;
only the measurement changed. Bun's own reporter emits no branch data at all
and its headline figure is an unweighted mean of per-file percentages, which
reads ~19 points high on this repo.
Baseline recorded 2026-09-07, the first honest measurement. Before the
test-shims/vscode package existed only 41 of 265 source files were reachable
from tests, and Bun reported 99.64% as an average over that 15% while the
whole VS Code integration layer was invisible rather than counted as zero.
All figures are WEIGHTED (hit/total across the repo), so they cannot be
nudged up by adding another tiny well-covered file.
Note these read LOWER than Bun's own figures (istanbul lines 14.23% vs Bun
24.61%). Istanbul counts every statement, including those inside functions
that are never called; Bun's line records are coarser. Istanbul's is the
stricter and more honest number, and it is the one gated.
2026-09-09: floors raised after editorHarness landed and sortCommands.ts
went 0% -> 100%. The harness fakes TextDocument/TextEditor with a real
edit() that applies its edits, which unlocks the ~200 command files that
all share that shape.
2026-09-09 (2): the five modules whose tests MIRRORED their logic rather
than importing it are now all at 100% - sortCommands, outlineProvider,
searchCommands, exportCommands, semanticProvider. Six more test files still
mirror; see the PR for the list.
2026-09-10: tabHandler.ts 0.9% -> 100% statements / 94.5% branches.
Its three uncovered branches are TYPE-NARROWING guards whose false path is
unreachable at runtime: getChevronLines only returns lines that already
parsed as bullet or numbered, so if(bullet) and if(chevrons) can never be
false - but TypeScript needs them to narrow string|undefined. First real
instance of literal-100% meeting an unreachable branch; flagged, not excluded.
